source_truth.answer: Barranco's century-old municipal library occupies the restored former municipal building on Parque Municipal and remains an operating public library.

original_spatial_contract.answer: A symmetrical civic façade and central portico organized municipal arrival; restored rooms now distribute reading, projection, children's and multipurpose programs.

current_life.answer: Users borrow, read, study, work and attend cultural/educational activity; current hours are published while coworking details require confirmation.

human_verbs_or_meaningful_absence.answer: Approach, enter, borrow, read, study, work, project and gather are credible. The decisive relation is park arrival becoming focused public learning through the portico.

architectural_causality.answer: Park frontage, central portico, vestibule and differentiated rooms turn an exterior civic ensemble into an interior sequence of quiet and collective uses.

visual_forensic_saturation.answer: Frontal symmetrical façade and empty restored-room coverage dominate. The underused frame connects the active park threshold to a real reading/work destination.

light_material_geometry.answer: Soft daylight can carry the portico-to-room depth; interior side light can separate restored openings, shelves and a reader without reducing the scene to décor.

position_then_optics.answer: Test park-side oblique, portico threshold and approved reading-room doorway. Start 35 mm for park/building depth, 50 mm for reader/threshold causality and 85 mm only across an authorized layered room.

moment_logistics_ethics.answer: Reconfirm hours and photography, avoid readable documents and identifiable children, keep silence/circulation, and fall back to public park/portico if interior work is declined.

one_frame_contest_test.answer: The frame passes when the former civic building visibly channels present reading or work. Heritage façade, generic library interior or event documentation alone fails.

source_truth.answer: Iglesia Santísima Cruz is Barranco's active parish church on Parque Municipal, with a neobaroque façade, Latin-cross interior and exterior oratories.

original_spatial_contract.answer: Built as the district's replacement worship center after damage to the older Ermita, it concentrates parish ritual at the civic core through nave, portico and exterior devotional points.

current_life.answer: The archdiocese lists it as a current parish; worship, prayer and parish organization are credible, but current cadence must be confirmed directly.

human_verbs_or_meaningful_absence.answer: Approach, cross, enter, pray, gather, wait and depart are credible. The decisive relation is private devotion or communal arrival occurring at the public civic edge.

architectural_causality.answer: Exterior oratories, central portico, nave hierarchy and barrel-vaulted interior graduate movement from open park to concentrated worship.

visual_forensic_saturation.answer: Centered façade, saint niches and empty nave dominate. The underused frame links exterior devotion or arrival with the civic park and deeper ritual axis.

light_material_geometry.answer: Garúa can reduce colorful civic clutter; low light can articulate façade relief, portico depth and the darker nave without turning worship into spectacle.

position_then_optics.answer: Test park-side lateral oratory, portico diagonal and approved nave threshold. Start 50 mm for worshipper/device, 35 mm for park-to-nave depth and 85 mm only from a respectful distant position.

moment_logistics_ethics.answer: Contact the parish for current schedule/photography, never disrupt liturgy or photograph vulnerable devotion closely, avoid flash and use exterior civic-edge fallback if interior work is declined.

one_frame_contest_test.answer: The frame passes when church thresholds visibly convert civic-space movement into present ritual. Symmetrical façade, worshipper scale or caption-dependent Ermita history fails.

source_truth.answer: Calle Porta is a seven-block Miraflores street descending from Schell toward the coast, historically lined with balneario houses and now strongly verticalized.

original_spatial_contract.answer: Low detached or semi-detached summer houses addressed a walkable street through doors, gardens and human-scale frontage along the coastal slope.

current_life.answer: Residents, workers, pedestrians and vehicles now occupy a mixed low/high corridor; current surviving fabric, works and thresholds require a full block walk.

human_verbs_or_meaningful_absence.answer: Exit, enter, walk, deliver, wait, overlook and demolish/build are credible. The strongest relation is simultaneous domestic-scale entry and tower-scale circulation.

architectural_causality.answer: Lot width, setback, garden wall, doorway, tower podium and street slope produce contrasting relations between dwelling, sidewalk and skyline.

visual_forensic_saturation.answer: Nostalgic isolated casona and generic tower canyon views dominate. The underused frame requires a surviving threshold and verticalized neighbor to share one active street plane.

light_material_geometry.answer: Garúa equalizes old/new surfaces and emphasizes scale; low side light can reveal setback, party wall and tower shadow crossing the smaller frontage.

position_then_optics.answer: Walk all seven blocks and test opposite curb, same-side slope and distant axial view only after confirming a surviving low/high pair. Start 50 mm for threshold/vertical plane, 35 mm for street section and 85 mm only if distance preserves shared frontage.

moment_logistics_ethics.answer: Verify construction and sidewalk access, never enter private property or photograph residents through windows, work from safe public pavement and kill any block lacking a current same-frame relation.

one_frame_contest_test.answer: The frame passes when built scale visibly changes present inhabitation at one shared street edge. Old-house portrait, tower spectacle or archival before/after requiring caption fails.
